_meta.purpose: Maps signals to a Flowcode product, a play, and a case study. The RANK stage reads this file. Pipeline code checks every product, play and case-study id the model returns against it.
_meta.rule: Quotes are copied exactly from flowcode.com. Metrics are written exactly as the case-study page shows them. Do not round or reword them.

products.name: Flowcodes
products.page_quote: Drive conversions in the real world with the #1 Enterprise QR code.
products.what_it_does: Dynamic, branded QR codes for physical touchpoints. The destination can be changed after printing. Every code is measured on its own and by location.
products.use_when: The brand has a physical or broadcast touchpoint (pack, shelf, display, OOH, TV spot, venue signage, merch) with no measurable digital next step.

products.name: FlowURLs
products.page_quote: FlowURLs connect your digital marketing to your real-world marketing
products.what_it_does: Branded, trackable short links with dynamic routing and IDs, for digital and social channels.
products.use_when: The brand runs social, influencer, email or digital campaigns and needs attribution tied to the same identity as its offline touchpoints.

products.name: FlowHubs
products.page_quote: Deliver personalized offers, apps, promotions, and sponsor ads straight from your brand ecosystem.
products.what_it_does: Mobile landing pages and campaign hubs, built from templates or fully custom. Routes each visitor to the right offer, content or action.
products.use_when: A campaign has several destinations (sweepstakes, recipe, store locator, app, sponsor offer) and needs one branded mobile destination.

products.name: FlowID & Personalization
products.page_quote: Build a persistent first-party identity from every Flowcode, FlowURL, and FlowHub connection.
products.what_it_does: Persistent first-party identity, two-way CRM sync, Smart Rules that route by loyalty tier, LTV or audience, and Audience Builder.
products.use_when: The brand has a loyalty, rewards or CRM program, or a touchpoint that reaches people but captures no first-party data.

products.name: Analytics & Integrations
products.page_quote: Real-time analytics that feed directly into your tech stack
products.what_it_does: Real-time dashboards, a Conversion Pixel for full-funnel attribution, SmartFlow (AI-driven optimization of landing experiences), and integrations with HubSpot, Salesforce, Snowflake, Adobe, Mailchimp, Zapier, Okta and Microsoft 365.
products.use_when: The brand spends heavily on offline media (TV, OOH, retail, sponsorships) and cannot measure which placements or creative drive results.

case_studies.what_they_did: Flowcodes on snack packaging led to a 'Snap, Scan, Win' giveaway, CRM sign-up and online purchase.
Flowcodes on beverage packaging led to sustainability content and an email sign-up for CRM capture.
Flowcodes on packaging unlocked digital games and rewards during a four-month U.S. campaign.
A scannable code on the front of the pack led to a sweepstakes entry for a Nintendo Switch 2 prize pack.
metrics: Top 3 performing code across the Kraft Heinz portfolio

case_studies.what_they_did: A Flowcode in the 2023 Super Bowl ad ('The Roast of Mr. Peanut', with VaynerMedia) led to long-form YouTube content.
metrics: 76% viewed full length content from ad

case_studies.what_they_did: Flowcodes inside a TV broadcast spot sent viewers straight to the NFL Shop store to buy.
A scannable Flowcode in an interactive TV commercial across several networks drove a Welch's Fruit Snacks sweepstakes with NFL player Mark Andrews. Real-time data was used to shift media placements.
A branded short-URL experience in digital channels led to a landing page with a sweepstakes and email opt-in form.
API-generated dynamic Flowcodes on in-store hang tags opened mobile product pages with fit, reviews and real-time inventory.
Flowcodes on airport kiosks and signage let travelers download the app or enroll on the spot.
QR codes on all merchandise and tickets for a concert tour drove exclusive-merch purchases and sweepstakes entries in exchange for fan emails.
metrics: $1.8M incremental tour revenue from merch sales

case_studies.what_they_did: In-arena Flowcodes drove sweepstakes entries, a 20% merch discount by live read, and scratch-card prizes.
A citywide treasure hunt in Tampa: 20 hidden Flowcodes led to a branded FlowHub to claim tickets, and Smart Rules blocked duplicate entries.
An omnichannel sweepstakes ran QR codes and short URLs across fan events, TV coverage and social, with entries captured in FlowID.

plays.name: On-pack conversion funnel
plays.play: Put a Flowcode on the pack that leads to a FlowHub (sweepstakes, recipe, game, store locator). Capture each scanner into FlowID and sync to the CRM. The code's destination can change after printing, so one print run supports later campaigns.

plays.name: Scannable TV and broadcast spots
plays.play: Put a Flowcode in the spot that leads to shop, content or a sweepstakes. Use analytics to see which creative and which network drove scans, then shift media spend.

plays.name: Event and sponsorship capture
plays.play: Put Flowcodes on signage, merch, tickets and activations that lead to a sponsor FlowHub. Use Smart Rules to block duplicate entries, and keep every fan as a first-party contact instead of leaving them with the rights holder.

plays.name: Retail shelf, display and tag
plays.play: Put Flowcodes on displays, shelf strips and tags that open a product page, retailer checkout or offer. Use analytics by location to see which stores and displays work.

plays.name: Measurable OOH and print
plays.play: Give each placement its own Flowcode so analytics show which locations convert. The destination can change without reprinting.

plays.name: Branded links for social and creators
plays.play: Use FlowURLs in creator and social posts that lead to the same FlowHub and FlowID as the offline touchpoints, so the brand can attribute digital and physical activity to the same people.

plays.name: Loyalty and first-party identity
plays.play: Turn every physical touchpoint into a loyalty or email sign-up through FlowID with two-way CRM sync. Use Smart Rules to route known members by tier and new visitors to enrollment.

scoring.formula: score = confidence x size x timing, each scored 1 to 5. The pipeline code multiplies and normalizes to 0-100. The model never computes the score.

confidence.5: Brand's own announcement (newsroom, press release, filing) or 2+ agreeing signals, AND the case study is a close match (same channel, similar category)
confidence.4: Strong evidence with a decent case-study match, or the brand's own source with a loose match
confidence.3: One secondary source, or the case study is only a loose analogy
confidence.2: Indirect evidence; Flowcode fit plausible but unproven

size.5: National or global reach: national TV, packaging on a national brand, a major league or tentpole sponsorship
size.4: Multi-market campaign or a major retailer partnership
size.3: A single large market, or a mid-size program

timing._meaning: Is there still time for Flowcode to get on this touchpoint? Not whether the campaign is live.
timing.5: The next touchpoint is still open: launching in 1-3 months, a sponsorship mid-season, or a recurring campaign whose next run is not produced yet
timing.4: Live now and still changeable (digital, event signage, a TV flight that is still buying), or a recurring item whose next run is 3-6 months out
timing.3: Already printed or produced for this season (packaging on shelves); the realistic pitch is the next run
timing.2: Just ended; recurs yearly, so pitch next year
timing.1: Over, with no sign it will recur

scoring.notes: Mention in the rationale if the brand already uses QR codes or links (an easier sale, possibly a competitor to replace) or if the touchpoint captures no first-party data (the gap FlowID fills). These shape confidence and the pitch. They are not separate multipliers.
